sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:7

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:7:1
items.html: These things proceed by degree: That is to say, the cascading proceeds according to the order of the degree of the coarseness that is in the screen. For there are in it five phases of coarseness, which are discerned according to the Sefirot of direct light. And the first three phases, which are phase four, phase three and phase two, called Peh, Hotem, Ozen, are actual breaths, for they raise reflected light — which is called breath — in a measure that suffices for the emergence of a Partzuf with RTS [Rosh-Toch-Sof], and these are the three Partzufim Galgalta, AB and SAG of AK, as is known. However, phase one of coarseness does not raise a breath that would suffice for an expansion into the Guf, and it is therefore called by the name a thin look. And all the more so the aspect of the coarseness of the root, called Keter, which has no breath at all for an expansion of a Guf. Rather, through the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Einayim, phase one too becomes fit for the emergence of a Partzuf, which is the Partzuf called Nekudim, or BON. And likewise, through the ascent of the bottom Hey to Keter, meaning to the forehead, the aspect of the root of the screen too becomes fit for the emergence of a Partzuf, namely the Partzuf called the new MA, which is the ten Sefirot of Atzilut. Therefore this reflected light, which emerges upon the bottom Hey that rose to the forehead, is called only by the name a revelation of illumination, or a will, and not by the aspect of a breath or a look — to indicate that there is in it no actual coarseness, but only the aspect of the root of the coarseness, and it is therefore called a will. For the four phases of coarseness are the growth of the will to receive in the order of the degree, as is known, whereas the aspect of their root is the aspect of the will to bestow alone, as is known, and there is in it nothing of the will to receive, only that which is a root for them. It is therefore called simply a will, or Raava DeMitzcha [the will of the forehead]. Understand this very well.
